limitations: Parallel groups record explicit boundaries/counts in their workflow VM. Individual branch membership of agent/workflow calls is not inferred from overlap.
The existing one-child-level workflow execution limit is unchanged. P4 delegation/deeper composition remains separate.
Structure attempts are not transcript snapshots; historical call links require the captured native cache key to still match.
Individual provider retry errors/timestamps and independent file-change artifacts remain the next P3.3 slice; reviewer/developer grants remain P3.4.
Rebuild and deploy the fixed local evaluator runtime with the server; stdio protocol 1 is rejected. The host-daemon protocol is unchanged.
Docker uses deterministic model fixtures and stock Qwen CLI, not corporate harness authorization.
verificationNotes: The first Docker run reached direct evaluator isolation proofs, whose old exact ready-frame expectation lacked protocolVersion:2. The expectation now verifies the new handshake field alongside unchanged UID/HOME/cwd/credential checks.

The next run timed out in the unchanged ordinary manual-agent command fixture before workflow/trace scenarios. Logs showed event-loop stalls and oom_kill=0. Runtime code, timeouts and assertions were retained for retry.

A later run passed native trace/replay proofs and the browser hierarchy/worker navigation, then missed the Bob hanging-automation command proof with oom_kill=0. The deterministic model fixture used a global marker Set, allowing a repeated HTTP request to skip an unacknowledged tool call. It now derives completion from that conversation tool result; a real-database regression test verifies repeated requests before/after tool acknowledgement. Browser automation also asserts the saved task and distinct run identity before checking execution/cancellation.

With conversation-based model acknowledgement, Alice automation command/cancellation passed. A later workflow had a succeeded step but was still running when the unrelated 15-second DOM-result timeout expired (oom_kill=0). Browser checks now first await the terminal owned workflow through the limited API with an execution deadline and fail immediately on failed/cancelled, then retain the UI render check. Recovery/crash fixture commands explicitly hang on their first real execution only; subsequent attempts still execute/acknowledge the command rather than relying on the removed global model Set.

The next full run passed the complete production browser suite, including both users’ workflows and automations, then timed out in the existing saved native-maintenance startup recovery. Host-daemon logs recorded 99–115 second heartbeat gaps. No cause is claimed from those gaps alone. The fixture now includes its saved operation state in a recovery failure; the next run uses caffeinate -i to prevent idle system sleep while preserving timeouts/assertions.

The final composite passed all 63 Turbo tasks, production browser, warm restart and abrupt crash recovery in 785193 ms. The cgroup snapshot after browser completion reported oom_kill=0. This is an observed final-run result, not a claim that prior intermittent fixture/host delays are eliminated.
